title: Choose the visual world
question: Which direction makes the benchmark setup feel clearest and most credible? Compare the previews, then lock one in or re-roll.

options.label: Semiconductor Test Traveler
options.lineage: Semiconductor wafer test recipes and traveler sheets
options.thesis: A run begins as a precise recipe and ends as an honest measurement record.
options.viewport: A wide setup sheet leads into an exact 100-cell operation map; recent runs stay in a narrow status rail.
options.risk: Could imply physical hardware; database names and plain-language labels must stay in front.

raised.raise: Anchor operation weights to one labeled 100% scale so plotted proportions retain exact meaning.
Reserve the strongest accent for actions; status color always pairs with a readable state label.
Give run IDs a precise fixed-width treatment while keeping every control and state visibly named.
Hold history columns steady and keep status changes readable without character-by-character animation.
Keep the next valid step obvious as the form narrows, without making every region a sign.

options.label: Logic Analyzer
options.thesis: Show the configured workload as six measured channels on one shared scale.
options.viewport: A six-lane operation-mix instrument leads the screen; the editable setup follows directly beneath it, with recent runs in a quiet event list.
options.risk: A waveform can suggest live telemetry; the preview uses only the configured weights and never invents performance data.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding Bands
options.lineage: Segmented travel documents and airport gate boards
options.thesis: Literal configuration bands lead into a stable, plainly labeled run-status board.
options.viewport: Broad yellow bands label the configuration sections; a fixed-column Recent runs board remains alongside the form.
options.case: Fuses well: clear bands organize a real configuration task, and stable status rows fit run history; the travel metaphor is less native to database developers than a measurement instrument.
options.risk: Travel language can distract from the database operation; keep all product labels literal.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: A measured system plotted as points against a coordinate field.
options.viewport: The six operation weights are indexed against a common 100% field, with run setup and history held in explicit labels.
options.case: Product clarity loses: celestial coordinates and variable-star markers do not describe configuring a database benchmark.
options.kept: Give every measurement an explicit scale and preserve its numeric meaning.
options.risk: Star imagery would suggest data that the benchmark has not collected.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: A gentle form gives one obvious action and one idea per region.
options.viewport: The configuration becomes a single scrolling form with the run action kept near its controls.
options.case: Audience identification loses: the language is familiar but does not express the precision-workstation use scene.
options.kept: Reserve the strongest accent for the action that can actually be taken.
options.risk: Nested cards would make the dense configuration harder to scan.

options.label: Coded Catalog Sleeve
options.lineage: Peter Saville Factory Records catalog sleeves
options.thesis: Each run receives an exact identity and a restrained signal mark.
options.viewport: Run IDs become the index; selecting one reveals its literal adapter, settings, state, and results.
options.case: Product clarity loses: replacing visible labels with color codes makes setup and state harder to understand.
options.kept: Keep run identifiers visually distinct and use fixed-width figures only where they carry data.
options.risk: The graphic could become a poster and leave too little room for the real controls.

options.label: Split-Flap Status Board
options.thesis: Run status changes ripple across a fixed column grid.
options.viewport: A compact history board shows run ID, adapter, scenario, and state beside the setup form.
options.case: It repeats the gate-board structure and spends motion on a status change that polling may not time precisely.
options.kept: Keep the history's columns stable and label every state in text.
options.risk: Character-by-character updates can misstate a real status transition.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.thesis: A chain of clear decisions guides the operator to a valid run.
options.viewport: Configuration sections become wayfinding bands, with the next choice and run action kept prominent.
options.case: It offers a path through the form but has less value once the operator reaches results and comparisons.
options.kept: Show the next available action plainly and keep hierarchy consistent on narrow screens.
options.risk: Bright yellow on a dense screen can dominate the measurements.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar operations dashboard: configure on the left, inspect recent runs on the right.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional header, labeled form, primary action, and recent-run list with the exact current product content.
canonCard.risk: Recognizable, but difficult to distinguish from other benchmark tools.
